messages:
maya: FYI seeing a sharp uptick in chart frame drops on /dashboards since last night's canary. Heavy queries (multi-agg) now take 2-3x longer to first-paint, users report sparkline freezes. :eyes:

maya: Quick evidence: client timeline shows stalled parse at bundle-load, then large idle while waiting for prefetch responses. KV-prefetch hit rate dropped from 92% -> 48%.

maya: Logs (clipboard):
```
Client: widget-load /dashboards/:chartId
prefetch -> routing: prefer-nearby
edge-node: 10.3.4.21 status:429 x120
kv-prefetch miss -> fetch upstream (higher latency)
render: blocked waiting for data (1200ms)
```

tony: interesting, we rolled a routing tweak yesterday to bias prefetch to the nearest region to reduce cross-region refill latency. thought it would help overall.

srikanth: that change toggled prefer-nearby for prefetch requests only. it looks like one EU edge is overloaded and returning 429s on small bursts — so preferring it makes cache misses worse.

ui-jane: UI note: the telemetry client 2.0 was shipped in the same canary and it inlines an init chunk that bumped the chart bundle by ~40KB. combined with prefetch stalls, main-thread stays busy longer.

maya: putting the two together seems to explain the tail: slightly bigger bundle + prefetch misses -> longer JS parse + waiting on data = visible jank.

deploy-bot: deploy "canary/2025-05-12/prefetch-routing" finished at 2025-05-12T02:18:00Z by srikanth.

elaine: ops: that EU edge is recovering but quota enforcement is aggressive for prefetch endpoints. We had a config to protect real user requests by throttling prefetch when burst > 100/sec. can revert or raise soft limit.

tony: options: 1) revert prefer-nearby for prefetch (global fallback to round-robin) 2) raise prefetch quota on EU edge 3) lazy-load telemetry client or split it out of main bundle as a fast-follow chunk.

sam: from PM POV prefer a targeted quick mitigation (revert routing) so we can buy time and then ship a proper fix (split telemetry + quota tuning). users are complaining on support but not critical yet.

srikanth: I can push a rollback of routing policy to canary off in 10min. Tony can you coordinate quota bump with Elaine?

elaine: I can increase soft quota for prefetch on the EU edge to 250/sec for the next 24h; will monitor 429 rates.

ui-jane: i'll open a tiny patch to lazy-load telemetry client and prototype async import so main bundle size drops. i can ship a canary within the day.

tony: sounds good. after rollback we'll re-run the dashboard perf suite and check KV hit rates + LCP.

maya: thanks — low-priority followups: add metric where prefetch 429s are correlated to chart jank, and label routing policy changes in the console rollouts timeline so we can debug faster next time. :+1:

srikanth: rollback started. updating thread when done.

deploy-bot: deploy "canary/2025-05-12/prefetch-routing-rollback" started by srikanth.

srikanth: rollback complete at 1755555612. initial telemetry shows prefetch 429s dropped to near zero and KV hit rate creeping back to ~88%.

maya: early numbers look promising, chart LCP median down ~300ms on canary users. leaving open until we confirm on prod rollout.

sam: thanks team, please document the postmortem and add rollout notes.
